35-banana-radioactive.name: Radioactive Bananas
35-banana-radioactive.idea: Bananas are full of potassium, and a tiny part of it is radioactive potassium-40. The dose is so small scientists use it as a joke unit: the banana equivalent dose. You'd need about 10 million at once to get sick.
35-banana-radioactive.title: Your banana is RADIOACTIVE 🍌
35-banana-radioactive.hook: That banana in your kitchen is radioactive.
35-banana-radioactive.body: Bananas are full of potassium, and a tiny part of it is radioactive potassium-40. The dose is so small scientists use it as a joke unit: the banana equivalent dose. You'd need about 10 million at once to get sick.
sources: US EPA, Radiation sources and doses (potassium-40 in food) https://www.epa.gov/radiation/radiation-sources-and-doses
Health Physics Society, Ask the Experts: bananas and radiation https://hps.org/publicinformation/ate/

36-pistol-shrimp.name: Pistol Shrimp
36-pistol-shrimp.idea: The pistol shrimp snaps its claw so fast it fires a water jet. The bubble collapses with a bang louder than a gunshot and reaches about 4,700 °C for a split second, stunning its prey.
36-pistol-shrimp.title: This shrimp shoots bubbles HOTTER than the Sun's surface?!
36-pistol-shrimp.hook: This tiny shrimp makes a bubble nearly as hot as the Sun.
36-pistol-shrimp.body: The pistol shrimp snaps its claw so fast it fires a water jet. The bubble collapses with a bang louder than a gunshot and reaches about 4,700 °C for a split second, stunning its prey.
sources: Lohse et al., Nature (2001), snapping shrimp make flashing bubbles https://www.nature.com/articles/35097152
Versluis et al., Science (2000), how snapping shrimp snap https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.289.5487.2114

37-cleopatra-moon.name: Cleopatra And The Moon Landing
37-cleopatra-moon.idea: The Great Pyramid was finished around 2560 BC. Cleopatra was born about 69 BC, nearly 2,500 years later. The Moon landing came only about 2,000 years after her.
37-cleopatra-moon.title: Cleopatra lived closer to the MOON LANDING than the pyramids
37-cleopatra-moon.hook: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid.
37-cleopatra-moon.body: The Great Pyramid was finished around 2560 BC. Cleopatra was born about 69 BC, nearly 2,500 years later. The Moon landing came only about 2,000 years after her.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Pyramids of Giza https://www.britannica.com/topic/Pyramids-of-Giza
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Cleopatra https://www.britannica.com/biography/Cleopatra-queen-of-Egypt

38-tardigrade-space.name: Tardigrades In Space
38-tardigrade-space.idea: Tardigrades are smaller than a millimetre. In 2007 they rode the FOTON-M3 mission and sat exposed to open space. Many came back alive, and some laid eggs. Their trick: drying out and switching off until water returns.
38-tardigrade-space.title: This animal SURVIVED open space 🚀
38-tardigrade-space.hook: This tiny animal survived the vacuum of space.
38-tardigrade-space.body: Tardigrades are smaller than a millimetre. In 2007 they rode the FOTON-M3 mission and sat exposed to open space. Many came back alive, and some laid eggs. Their trick: drying out and switching off until water returns.
sources: Jönsson et al., Current Biology (2008), tardigrades survive exposure to space https://www.cell.com/current-biology/fulltext/S0960-9822(08)00805-1
European Space Agency, FOTON-M3 mission https://www.esa.int/

39-venus-day.name: Venus Day
39-venus-day.idea: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only 225 days to orbit the Sun. And it spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west.
39-venus-day.title: On Venus a DAY is longer than a YEAR
39-venus-day.hook: On Venus, one day lasts longer than a whole year.
39-venus-day.body: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only 225 days to orbit the Sun. And it spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west.
sources: NASA Science, Venus facts https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/
ESA, Venus Express: Venus rotation https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Venus_Express

40-hippo-swim.name: Hippos Can't Swim
40-hippo-swim.idea: They spend up to 16 hours a day in rivers but are too heavy to float. They walk and bounce along the bottom, hold their breath about 5 minutes, and even surface to breathe while asleep.
40-hippo-swim.title: Hippos CAN'T swim (here's what they do instead)
40-hippo-swim.hook: Hippos live in water, but they can't swim.
40-hippo-swim.body: They spend up to 16 hours a day in rivers but are too heavy to float. They walk and bounce along the bottom, hold their breath about 5 minutes, and even surface to breathe while asleep.
sources: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, Hippopotamus https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/hippo
National Geographic, Hippopotamus https://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/mammals/facts/hippopotamus

41-shortest-war.name: Shortest War
41-shortest-war.idea: In 1896 Britain and Zanzibar went to war after a new sultan took power without British approval. Ships opened fire at 9:00. By about 9:40 the palace was wrecked and the war was over.
41-shortest-war.title: The shortest war EVER lasted under 45 minutes
41-shortest-war.hook: The shortest war in history was over before breakfast.
41-shortest-war.body: In 1896 Britain and Zanzibar went to war after a new sultan took power without British approval. Ships opened fire at 9:00. By about 9:40 the palace was wrecked and the war was over.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Anglo-Zanzibar War https://www.britannica.com/event/Anglo-Zanzibar-War
Guinness World Records, Shortest war https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/shortest-war

42-scotland-unicorn.name: Scotland's Unicorn
42-scotland-unicorn.idea: Scottish kings put the unicorn on their royal arms over 500 years ago as a symbol of purity and power. Legend said only a king could tame one, which is why it wears a chain.
42-scotland-unicorn.title: Scotland's national animal is a UNICORN 🦄
42-scotland-unicorn.hook: Scotland's national animal is a unicorn. Seriously.
42-scotland-unicorn.body: Scottish kings put the unicorn on their royal arms over 500 years ago as a symbol of purity and power. Legend said only a king could tame one, which is why it wears a chain.
sources: VisitScotland, Why is the unicorn Scotland's national animal? https://www.visitscotland.com/
National Records of Scotland / Court of the Lord Lyon, Royal arms of Scotland https://www.courtofthelordlyon.scot/

43-nintendo-1889.name: Nintendo 1889
43-nintendo-1889.idea: It was founded in Kyoto in 1889 making hanafuda playing cards. It tried a taxi company and instant rice before toys, and only decades later video games like Super Mario.
43-nintendo-1889.title: Nintendo is 135 YEARS old (it didn't start with games) 🎮
43-nintendo-1889.body: It was founded in Kyoto in 1889 making hanafuda playing cards. It tried a taxi company and instant rice before toys, and only decades later video games like Super Mario.
sources: Nintendo, Company history https://www.nintendo.co.jp/corporate/en/history/index.html
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Nintendo https://www.britannica.com/topic/Nintendo-Company-Ltd

44-napoleon-height.name: Napoleon Wasn't Short
44-napoleon-height.idea: He was about 1.69 m (5 ft 7), average or a bit tall for a Frenchman then. Longer French inches got mistranslated, and British cartoonists loved drawing him tiny.
44-napoleon-height.title: Napoleon WASN'T short. The truth:
44-napoleon-height.hook: Napoleon wasn't short. History lied to you.
44-napoleon-height.body: He was about 1.69 m (5 ft 7), average or a bit tall for a Frenchman then. Longer French inches got mistranslated, and British cartoonists loved drawing him tiny.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Was Napoleon short? https://www.britannica.com/story/was-napoleon-short
Napoleon Foundation (fondationnapoleon.org), Napoleon's height https://www.napoleon.org/en/

45-butterfly-feet.name: Butterflies Taste With Feet
45-butterfly-feet.idea: Their feet are covered in taste sensors. A female drums a leaf with her feet to taste it, and only lays eggs if it is the right food plant for her caterpillars.
45-butterfly-feet.title: Butterflies TASTE with their FEET
45-butterfly-feet.body: Their feet are covered in taste sensors. A female drums a leaf with her feet to taste it, and only lays eggs if it is the right food plant for her caterpillars.
sources: Smithsonian, Butterflies taste with their feet https://www.si.edu/
Briscoe et al., PNAS (2013), gustatory receptors in Heliconius butterfly legs https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1302186110

46-neutron-spoon.name: Neutron Star Spoon
46-neutron-spoon.idea: A neutron star is the crushed core of an exploded giant star. It squeezes more mass than the Sun into a ball about 20 km wide. A spoonful dropped on Earth would punch straight through the ground.
46-neutron-spoon.title: 1 teaspoon of this star weighs a BILLION tonnes
46-neutron-spoon.hook: One teaspoon of this star weighs a billion tonnes.
46-neutron-spoon.body: A neutron star is the crushed core of an exploded giant star. It squeezes more mass than the Sun into a ball about 20 km wide. A spoonful dropped on Earth would punch straight through the ground.
sources: NASA Goddard, Neutron stars https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/science/objects/neutron_stars1.html
NASA, NICER mission: neutron star size https://www.nasa.gov/nicer/

47-trees-stars.name: Trees vs Stars
47-trees-stars.idea: About 3 trillion trees grow on Earth, counted with satellites and forest surveys. The Milky Way has 100 to 400 billion stars. That's several trees per star.
47-trees-stars.title: Earth has MORE trees than the galaxy has stars
47-trees-stars.hook: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy.
47-trees-stars.body: About 3 trillion trees grow on Earth, counted with satellites and forest surveys. The Milky Way has 100 to 400 billion stars. That's several trees per star.
sources: Crowther et al., Nature (2015), mapping tree density at a global scale https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14967
NASA, How many stars in the Milky Way? https://science.nasa.gov/

48-ketchup-medicine.name: Ketchup Medicine
48-ketchup-medicine.idea: In the 1830s Dr John Cook Bennett claimed tomatoes cured indigestion. Companies sold tomato pills promising to fix almost anything, until fakes and wild claims ended the craze.
48-ketchup-medicine.title: Ketchup was sold as MEDICINE 💊
48-ketchup-medicine.hook: Ketchup used to be sold as medicine.
48-ketchup-medicine.body: In the 1830s Dr John Cook Bennett claimed tomatoes cured indigestion. Companies sold tomato pills promising to fix almost anything, until fakes and wild claims ended the craze.
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, Ketchup was once sold as medicine https://www.smithsonianmag.com/
Andrew F. Smith, The Tomato in America (University of South Carolina Press, 1994)

49-empire-lightning.name: Empire State Lightning
49-empire-lightning.idea: The Empire State Building's steel spire acts like a giant lightning rod, catching bolts and sending them safely to the ground. It was once struck 8 times in 24 minutes.
49-empire-lightning.title: Lightning never strikes twice? WRONG ⚡
49-empire-lightning.hook: Lightning never strikes twice? This building gets hit 20 times a year.
49-empire-lightning.body: The Empire State Building's steel spire acts like a giant lightning rod, catching bolts and sending them safely to the ground. It was once struck 8 times in 24 minutes.
sources: US National Weather Service, Lightning myths https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-myths
Empire State Building, Facts https://www.esbnyc.com/

50-saturn-float.name: Saturn Would Float
50-saturn-float.idea: It's huge but mostly hydrogen and helium, so on average it's less dense than water. In a big enough bathtub it would bob like a rubber duck. Good luck finding the tub.
50-saturn-float.title: Saturn would FLOAT in a bathtub 🪐
50-saturn-float.body: It's huge but mostly hydrogen and helium, so on average it's less dense than water. In a big enough bathtub it would bob like a rubber duck. Good luck finding the tub.
sources: NASA Science, Saturn facts https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/
NASA Space Place, All about Saturn https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/all-about-saturn/en/

51-mantis-punch.name: Mantis Shrimp Punch
51-mantis-punch.idea: The mantis shrimp swings its club so fast the water boils into bubbles. When they collapse they hit the prey again with heat and light. It can crack aquarium glass.
51-mantis-punch.title: This shrimp punches like a BULLET 🥊
51-mantis-punch.hook: This shrimp punches with the acceleration of a bullet.
51-mantis-punch.body: The mantis shrimp swings its club so fast the water boils into bubbles. When they collapse they hit the prey again with heat and light. It can crack aquarium glass.
sources: Patek, Korff & Caldwell, Nature (2004), deadly strike of the mantis shrimp https://www.nature.com/articles/428819a
Natural History Museum (London), Mantis shrimp https://www.nhm.ac.uk/

52-polar-bear-skin.name: Polar Bears Aren't White
52-polar-bear-skin.idea: Their skin is black to soak up warmth. Each hair is clear and hollow and scatters light, so the fur only looks white.
52-polar-bear-skin.title: Polar bears AREN'T white 🐻‍❄️
52-polar-bear-skin.body: Their skin is black to soak up warmth. Each hair is clear and hollow and scatters light, so the fur only looks white.
sources: Polar Bears International, Polar bear facts https://polarbearsinternational.org/polar-bears-changing-arctic/polar-bear-facts/
Smithsonian's National Zoo, Why are polar bears white? https://nationalzoo.si.edu/

53-crows-faces.name: Crows Remember Faces
53-crows-faces.idea: University of Washington scientists wore a mask while catching crows. For years, crows scolded anyone in that mask, even crows that never saw the capture, because others taught them.
53-crows-faces.title: Crows NEVER forget your face 👀
53-crows-faces.hook: Crows never forget your face, and they hold grudges.
53-crows-faces.body: University of Washington scientists wore a mask while catching crows. For years, crows scolded anyone in that mask, even crows that never saw the capture, because others taught them.
sources: Marzluff et al., Animal Behaviour (2010), lasting recognition of threatening people by wild crows https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0003347209005806
University of Washington News, Crows remember human faces https://www.washington.edu/news/

54-great-fire.name: Great Fire Of London
54-great-fire.idea: The fire started in a bakery on Pudding Lane in 1666 and destroyed over 13,000 homes, St Paul's Cathedral and 87 churches. Only 6 deaths were recorded; historians think there were many more.
54-great-fire.title: The Great Fire of London: only 6 deaths? NOT true
54-great-fire.hook: London burned for 4 days, and the death toll is a mystery.
54-great-fire.body: The fire started in a bakery on Pudding Lane in 1666 and destroyed over 13,000 homes, St Paul's Cathedral and 87 churches. Only 6 deaths were recorded; historians think there were many more.
sources: Museum of London, The Great Fire of London https://www.museumoflondon.org.uk/
UK National Archives, Great Fire of London https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/resources/great-fire-of-london/

55-pineapple-years.name: Pineapples Take 2 Years
55-pineapple-years.idea: Each plant makes one pineapple at a time, and it isn't one fruit: it's dozens of berries fused around a stem.
55-pineapple-years.title: A pineapple takes 2 YEARS to grow 🍍
55-pineapple-years.hook: A pineapple takes about two years to grow.
55-pineapple-years.body: Each plant makes one pineapple at a time, and it isn't one fruit: it's dozens of berries fused around a stem.
sources: University of Hawaii CTAHR, Pineapple growing https://www.ctahr.hawaii.edu/
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Pineapple https://www.britannica.com/plant/pineapple

56-fingernails.name: Fingernails vs Toenails
56-fingernails.idea: Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month, so a whole nail is replaced in ~6 months. Toenails can take over a year. Hands get more blood flow and more knocks.
56-fingernails.title: Your fingernails grow 2x FASTER than toenails
56-fingernails.hook: Your fingernails grow twice as fast as your toenails.
56-fingernails.body: Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month, so a whole nail is replaced in ~6 months. Toenails can take over a year. Hands get more blood flow and more knocks.
sources: American Academy of Dermatology, Nail facts https://www.aad.org/
Yaemsiri et al., J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol (2010), growth rate of human fingernails and toenails https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20030633/

57-sound-water.name: Sound In Water
57-sound-water.idea: In air it moves about 340 m/s. In water, nearly 1,500 m/s, because packed molecules pass the vibration quicker. That's how whales call across oceans.
57-sound-water.title: Sound is 4x FASTER underwater 🐋
57-sound-water.hook: Sound travels over four times faster in water than in air.
57-sound-water.body: In air it moves about 340 m/s. In water, nearly 1,500 m/s, because packed molecules pass the vibration quicker. That's how whales call across oceans.
sources: NOAA Ocean Service, How far does sound travel in the ocean? https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/sound.html
Discovery of Sound in the Sea (University of Rhode Island) https://dosits.org/

58-rain-smell.name: Smell Of Rain
58-rain-smell.idea: It's petrichor. Most of it is geosmin, made by soil bacteria. Raindrops fling it into the air, and your nose can detect just a few drops of it in a swimming pool.
58-rain-smell.title: That smell after rain has a NAME
58-rain-smell.hook: That smell after rain has a name.
58-rain-smell.body: It's petrichor. Most of it is geosmin, made by soil bacteria. Raindrops fling it into the air, and your nose can detect just a few drops of it in a swimming pool.
sources: Bear & Thomas, Nature (1964), nature of argillaceous odour https://www.nature.com/articles/201993a0
MIT News (2015), Rain releases aerosols https://news.mit.edu/2015/rainfall-can-release-aerosols-0114

59-sloth-breath.name: Sloths Hold Breath
59-sloth-breath.idea: They slow their heartbeat to save oxygen. And surprise: sloths are good swimmers, about three times faster in water than on land.
59-sloth-breath.title: Sloths hold their breath LONGER than dolphins
59-sloth-breath.hook: Sloths can hold their breath for 40 minutes.
59-sloth-breath.body: They slow their heartbeat to save oxygen. And surprise: sloths are good swimmers, about three times faster in water than on land.
sources: Sloth Conservation Foundation, Sloth facts https://slothconservation.org/
WWF, Sloth https://www.worldwildlife.org/species/sloth

60-moon-away.name: Moon Running Away
60-moon-away.idea: It drifts about 3.8 cm further every year, about as fast as fingernails grow. We measure it by bouncing lasers off mirrors Apollo astronauts left. Our days are slowly getting longer too.
60-moon-away.title: The Moon is RUNNING AWAY from us 🌙
60-moon-away.hook: The Moon is running away from Earth.
60-moon-away.body: It drifts about 3.8 cm further every year, about as fast as fingernails grow. We measure it by bouncing lasers off mirrors Apollo astronauts left. Our days are slowly getting longer too.
sources: NASA, Apollo 11 laser ranging retroreflector https://science.nasa.gov/
NASA Solar System Exploration, Moon facts https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/

61-antarctica-desert.name: Antarctica Desert
61-antarctica-desert.idea: It's Antarctica. A desert means very little rain or snow, and Antarctica gets less than many hot deserts. Some Dry Valleys haven't seen rain in thousands of years.
61-antarctica-desert.title: The biggest desert is NOT the Sahara
61-antarctica-desert.hook: The biggest desert on Earth isn't the Sahara.
61-antarctica-desert.body: It's Antarctica. A desert means very little rain or snow, and Antarctica gets less than many hot deserts. Some Dry Valleys haven't seen rain in thousands of years.
sources: NASA Earth Observatory, Antarctica's Dry Valleys https://earthobservatory.nasa.gov/
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Desert https://www.britannica.com/science/desert

62-cloud-weight.name: Clouds Weigh Tonnes
62-cloud-weight.idea: That's like 100 elephants floating overhead. The water is split into trillions of tiny droplets spread across a huge space, and rising warm air holds them up until they grow and fall as rain.
62-cloud-weight.title: A cloud weighs as much as 100 ELEPHANTS ☁️
62-cloud-weight.hook: A fluffy cloud can weigh 500 tonnes.
62-cloud-weight.body: That's like 100 elephants floating overhead. The water is split into trillions of tiny droplets spread across a huge space, and rising warm air holds them up until they grow and fall as rain.
sources: USGS Water Science School, How much does a cloud weigh? https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school
NOAA SciJinks, Why do clouds float? https://scijinks.gov/

63-elephant-jump.name: Elephants Can't Jump
63-elephant-jump.idea: All four feet never leave the ground at once. Their leg bones point straight down and their ankles aren't springy. Even running, one foot always stays down.
63-elephant-jump.title: Elephants CAN'T jump. Not even a little 🐘
63-elephant-jump.body: All four feet never leave the ground at once. Their leg bones point straight down and their ankles aren't springy. Even running, one foot always stays down.
sources: Hutchinson et al., Nature (2003), are fast-moving elephants really running? https://www.nature.com/articles/422493a
San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, Elephant https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/elephant

64-dolphin-sleep.name: Dolphins Half Asleep
64-dolphin-sleep.idea: One side rests while the other stays alert, and one eye stays open. They keep swimming, breathing and watching for sharks, then the sides swap.
64-dolphin-sleep.title: Dolphins sleep with HALF their brain 🐬
64-dolphin-sleep.hook: Dolphins sleep with half their brain awake.
64-dolphin-sleep.body: One side rests while the other stays alert, and one eye stays open. They keep swimming, breathing and watching for sharks, then the sides swap.
sources: Rattenborg et al., Neurosci Biobehav Rev (2000), unihemispheric sleep https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11033047/
Scientific American, How do dolphins sleep? https://www.scientificamerican.com/

65-mammoth-pyramids.name: Mammoths And Pyramids
65-mammoth-pyramids.idea: The pyramid went up around 2560 BC. A small group of mammoths survived on Wrangel Island off Siberia until about 2000 BC, centuries later.
65-mammoth-pyramids.title: Mammoths were ALIVE when the pyramids were built
65-mammoth-pyramids.hook: Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
65-mammoth-pyramids.body: The pyramid went up around 2560 BC. A small group of mammoths survived on Wrangel Island off Siberia until about 2000 BC, centuries later.
sources: Vartanyan et al., Nature (1993), Holocene dwarf mammoths from Wrangel Island https://www.nature.com/articles/362337a0
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Pyramids of Giza https://www.britannica.com/topic/Pyramids-of-Giza

66-hummingbird-backwards.name: Hummingbirds Fly Backwards
66-hummingbird-backwards.idea: They twist their wings in a figure eight, getting lift on the downstroke and the upstroke. Some beat about 80 times a second, so they can hover, go sideways and reverse.
66-hummingbird-backwards.title: The ONLY bird that flies BACKWARDS
66-hummingbird-backwards.body: They twist their wings in a figure eight, getting lift on the downstroke and the upstroke. Some beat about 80 times a second, so they can hover, go sideways and reverse.
sources: Warrick, Tobalske & Powers, Nature (2005), aerodynamics of the hovering hummingbird https://www.nature.com/articles/nature03647
Smithsonian's National Zoo, Hummingbird facts https://nationalzoo.si.edu/

67-heart-beats.name: Heart Beats
67-heart-beats.idea: That's around 35 million beats a year and over 2.5 billion in a lifetime. It pushes blood through about 100,000 km of vessels, enough to wrap Earth more than twice.
67-heart-beats.title: Your heart beats 100,000 times A DAY ❤️
67-heart-beats.hook: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
67-heart-beats.body: That's around 35 million beats a year and over 2.5 billion in a lifetime. It pushes blood through about 100,000 km of vessels, enough to wrap Earth more than twice.
sources: American Heart Association, How the heart works https://www.heart.org/
Franklin Institute, Blood vessels: the circulatory system https://www.fi.edu/en/science-and-education/your-heart

68-purple-carrots.name: Purple Carrots
68-purple-carrots.idea: The first farmed carrots in Central Asia were purple and yellow. Orange carrots took off in the Netherlands in the 1600s. The William of Orange story is probably a myth.
68-purple-carrots.title: Carrots were PURPLE before orange 🥕
68-purple-carrots.hook: Carrots didn't used to be orange.
68-purple-carrots.body: The first farmed carrots in Central Asia were purple and yellow. Orange carrots took off in the Netherlands in the 1600s. The William of Orange story is probably a myth.
sources: World Carrot Museum, History of carrot colours http://www.carrotmuseum.co.uk/history.html
Smithsonian Magazine, Why are carrots orange? https://www.smithsonianmag.com/

69-spider-silk.name: Spider Silk Vs Steel
69-spider-silk.idea: Weight for weight, some silk beats steel and is tougher than Kevlar. Darwin's bark spider makes the toughest silk known and spins webs across rivers up to 25 m wide.
69-spider-silk.title: Spider silk is STRONGER than steel 🕷️
69-spider-silk.hook: Spider silk is stronger than steel.
69-spider-silk.body: Weight for weight, some silk beats steel and is tougher than Kevlar. Darwin's bark spider makes the toughest silk known and spins webs across rivers up to 25 m wide.
sources: Agnarsson et al., PLoS ONE (2010), bioprospecting finds the toughest biological material https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0011234
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Spider silk https://www.britannica.com/

70-glass-frog.name: Glass Frog
70-glass-frog.idea: Glass frogs have transparent bellies. When they sleep they hide most red blood cells in their liver, becoming up to 61% more transparent so birds look right through them.
70-glass-frog.title: This frog is SEE-THROUGH 🐸
70-glass-frog.hook: You can see this frog's heart beating through its belly.
70-glass-frog.body: Glass frogs have transparent bellies. When they sleep they hide most red blood cells in their liver, becoming up to 61% more transparent so birds look right through them.
sources: Taboada et al., Science (2022), glassfrogs conceal blood in their liver https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abl6620
Duke University News (2022), glass frogs hide red blood cells https://today.duke.edu/

71-viking-helmets.name: Viking Helmets
71-viking-helmets.idea: The only nearly complete Viking helmet, the Gjermundbu helmet, has no horns. The horns came from Carl Emil Doepler's costumes for Wagner's Ring cycle in 1876.
71-viking-helmets.title: Vikings NEVER wore horned helmets
71-viking-helmets.body: The only nearly complete Viking helmet, the Gjermundbu helmet, has no horns. The horns came from Carl Emil Doepler's costumes for Wagner's Ring cycle in 1876.
sources: Museum of Cultural History, University of Oslo, Gjermundbu helmet https://www.khm.uio.no/english/
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Did Vikings wear horned helmets? https://www.britannica.com/story/did-vikings-really-wear-horns-on-their-helmets

72-koala-fingerprints.name: Koala Fingerprints
72-koala-fingerprints.idea: Even experts struggle to tell them apart under a microscope: same loops and swirls. Koalas aren't close relatives, so the prints evolved separately for grip and feeling leaves.
72-koala-fingerprints.title: Koala fingerprints look EXACTLY like ours 🐨
72-koala-fingerprints.hook: Koalas have fingerprints almost identical to ours.
72-koala-fingerprints.body: Even experts struggle to tell them apart under a microscope: same loops and swirls. Koalas aren't close relatives, so the prints evolved separately for grip and feeling leaves.
sources: Henneberg, Lambert & Leigh, Nature (1996), fingerprint homoplasy: koalas and humans https://www.nature.com/articles/382205a0
Australian Koala Foundation, Koala facts https://www.savethekoala.com/

73-bee-faces.name: Bees Recognise Faces
73-bee-faces.idea: In a 2005 study, bees trained with sugar water picked out one face photo from several, and still remembered it two days later. They piece faces together like a puzzle.
73-bee-faces.title: Bees can RECOGNISE your face 🐝
73-bee-faces.hook: Honeybees can learn to recognise human faces.
73-bee-faces.body: In a 2005 study, bees trained with sugar water picked out one face photo from several, and still remembered it two days later. They piece faces together like a puzzle.
sources: Dyer, Neumeyer & Chittka, J Exp Biol (2005), honeybee face recognition https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/article/208/24/4709/16068
Avarguès-Weber et al., J Exp Biol (2010), configural processing in honeybees https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/

74-flamingo-pink.name: Flamingos Born Grey
74-flamingo-pink.idea: Their food, algae and tiny shrimp, is full of carotenoid pigments that colour their feathers. Stop eating them and the pink fades, so zoos add pigment to their food.
74-flamingo-pink.title: Flamingos are born GREY 🦩
74-flamingo-pink.body: Their food, algae and tiny shrimp, is full of carotenoid pigments that colour their feathers. Stop eating them and the pink fades, so zoos add pigment to their food.
sources: Smithsonian's National Zoo, Flamingo facts https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/american-flamingo
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Flamingo https://www.britannica.com/animal/flamingo

75-mars-sunset.name: Blue Mars Sunset
75-mars-sunset.idea: Fine Martian dust lets blue light through near the Sun while other colours scatter. The daytime sky is butterscotch, but sunset glows blue. NASA rovers have photographed it many times.
75-mars-sunset.title: Sunsets on Mars are BLUE 🔵
75-mars-sunset.body: Fine Martian dust lets blue light through near the Sun while other colours scatter. The daytime sky is butterscotch, but sunset glows blue. NASA rovers have photographed it many times.
sources: NASA JPL, Curiosity captures blue sunset on Mars https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/images/pia19400-sunset-in-mars-gale-crater
NASA Science, Mars facts https://science.nasa.gov/mars/facts/

76-red-spot.name: Great Red Spot
76-red-spot.idea: The Great Red Spot has been watched for 190+ years, with winds over 600 km/h. But it's shrinking: a century ago it fit about 3 Earths, now just over 1.
76-red-spot.title: A storm BIGGER than Earth is dying
76-red-spot.hook: There's a storm on Jupiter bigger than the whole Earth.
76-red-spot.body: The Great Red Spot has been watched for 190+ years, with winds over 600 km/h. But it's shrinking: a century ago it fit about 3 Earths, now just over 1.
sources: NASA Science, Jupiter's Great Red Spot https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/
NASA/ESA Hubble, Great Red Spot is shrinking https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/

77-owl-neck.name: Owl Neck
77-owl-neck.idea: Their eyes are fixed, so the head moves instead. They have 14 neck bones, twice ours, and blood pools that keep the brain fed while twisting. We'd tear our arteries.
77-owl-neck.title: Owls turn their heads 270° (DON'T try this) 🦉
77-owl-neck.hook: Owls can turn their heads 270 degrees.
77-owl-neck.body: Their eyes are fixed, so the head moves instead. They have 14 neck bones, twice ours, and blood pools that keep the brain fed while twisting. We'd tear our arteries.
sources: de Kok-Mercado et al., Science (2013), adaptations in owls for head rotation https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.339.6119.514
Johns Hopkins Medicine (2013), how owls turn their heads https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/news/

78-hiccups-68-years.name: 68 Years Of Hiccups
78-hiccups-68-years.idea: Charles Osborne started hiccuping in 1922 while lifting a pig and didn't stop until 1990, an estimated 430 million hiccups. He still married twice and had eight children.
78-hiccups-68-years.title: This man had HICCUPS for 68 YEARS
78-hiccups-68-years.hook: One man had hiccups for 68 years.
78-hiccups-68-years.body: Charles Osborne started hiccuping in 1922 while lifting a pig and didn't stop until 1990, an estimated 430 million hiccups. He still married twice and had eight children.
sources: Guinness World Records, Longest attack of hiccups https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/longest-attack-of-hiccups
Los Angeles Times (1991), Charles Osborne obituary https://www.latimes.com/

79-cacao-money.name: Chocolate Money
79-cacao-money.idea: Cacao beans were real currency: a turkey cost about 100 beans and an avocado about 3. Fakers filled empty shells with mud, and the rich drank their money as a spicy drink.
79-cacao-money.title: The Aztecs paid with CHOCOLATE 🍫
79-cacao-money.hook: The Aztecs used chocolate as money.
79-cacao-money.body: Cacao beans were real currency: a turkey cost about 100 beans and an avocado about 3. Fakers filled empty shells with mud, and the rich drank their money as a spicy drink.
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, A brief history of chocolate https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/a-brief-history-of-chocolate-21860917/
Sophie & Michael Coe, The True History of Chocolate (Thames & Hudson, 1996)

80-goldfish-memory.name: Goldfish Memory
80-goldfish-memory.idea: Experiments show they remember for months. They've been trained to push levers for food, swim to a sound, learn feeding times, and even swim through a small maze.
80-goldfish-memory.title: The 3-second goldfish memory is a MYTH 🐟
80-goldfish-memory.hook: Goldfish don't have a three-second memory.
80-goldfish-memory.body: Experiments show they remember for months. They've been trained to push levers for food, swim to a sound, learn feeding times, and even swim through a small maze.
sources: Plymouth University research on goldfish lever training (BBC News, 2003) https://news.bbc.co.uk/
Smithsonian Magazine, Goldfish memory myth https://www.smithsonianmag.com/

81-sun-mass.name: The Sun's Mass
81-sun-mass.idea: It's about 99.86% of the solar system's mass. Planets, moons, asteroids and comets share the rest, and Jupiter takes most of that. About 1.3 million Earths would fit inside the Sun.
81-sun-mass.title: The Sun is 99.86% of EVERYTHING ☀️
81-sun-mass.hook: The Sun holds almost all the stuff in our solar system.
81-sun-mass.body: It's about 99.86% of the solar system's mass. Planets, moons, asteroids and comets share the rest, and Jupiter takes most of that. About 1.3 million Earths would fit inside the Sun.
sources: NASA Science, Sun facts https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/
NASA Space Place, How big is the Sun? https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/

82-immortal-jellyfish.name: Immortal Jellyfish
82-immortal-jellyfish.idea: When hurt, old or starving, Turritopsis dohrnii turns back into a baby polyp and grows up again. In theory it can repeat forever; in the wild most get eaten, but not by old age.
82-immortal-jellyfish.title: This jellyfish can live FOREVER
82-immortal-jellyfish.hook: There's a jellyfish that can live forever.
82-immortal-jellyfish.body: When hurt, old or starving, Turritopsis dohrnii turns back into a baby polyp and grows up again. In theory it can repeat forever; in the wild most get eaten, but not by old age.
sources: Pascual-Torner et al., PNAS (2022), comparative genomics of Turritopsis dohrnii https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2118763119
American Museum of Natural History, The immortal jellyfish https://www.amnh.org/

83-oldest-tree.name: Methuselah Tree
83-oldest-tree.idea: Methuselah, a bristlecone pine in California's White Mountains, was already a few hundred years old when the Great Pyramid was built. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.
83-oldest-tree.title: This tree is OLDER than the pyramids 🌲
83-oldest-tree.hook: There's a tree that's over 4,800 years old.
83-oldest-tree.body: Methuselah, a bristlecone pine in California's White Mountains, was already a few hundred years old when the Great Pyramid was built. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.
sources: US Forest Service, Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest https://www.fs.usda.gov/recarea/inyo/recarea/?recid=20240
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Bristlecone pine https://www.britannica.com/plant/bristlecone-pine

84-stomach-lining.name: New Stomach Lining
84-stomach-lining.idea: Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve some metals, so lining cells wear out fast and are replaced every 3 to 5 days. Thick mucus coats the walls so your stomach doesn't digest itself.
84-stomach-lining.title: You get a NEW stomach lining every few days
84-stomach-lining.hook: Your stomach makes a new lining every few days.
84-stomach-lining.body: Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve some metals, so lining cells wear out fast and are replaced every 3 to 5 days. Thick mucus coats the walls so your stomach doesn't digest itself.
sources: Cleveland Clinic, Stomach: anatomy and function https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21758-stomach
Encyclopaedia Britannica, Stomach https://www.britannica.com/science/stomach
